any_of: requested more vCPU capacity than your current vCPU limit
required.rationale: the literal only the job log supplies

required.asked_by: explain why the request overflowed it
required.rationale: the synthesis: the sum from the catalog item compared against the limit from the log
required.note: common.yaml sets one m6i.xlarge bastion (4 vCPU), 3 m6i.2xlarge control nodes (8 vCPU) and 3 m6i.4xlarge workers (16 vCPU), 76 vCPU in total, and the job log gives the account's vCPU limit as 64.

counts.rationale: read from the log's AWS message

counts.asked_by: how many vCPUs the catalog item asks for
counts.rationale: a sum over three sizing lines in agnosticv common.yaml; only the fetch supplies the instance types and counts

citations.asked_by: cite the line that sets the worker instance size
citations.rationale: the line number is counted from the seeded file; it proves the agnosticv file, not the agnosticd defaults, was read

forbidden.rationale: the agnosticd config defaults (1 x m6i.2xlarge worker; 22 vCPU total: m6i.large 2 + 3 x m6i.xlarge 4 = 12 + m6i.2xlarge 8) are overridden by the catalog item; quoting them as the sizing is the wrong-file mistake. '44 vCPU' is kept as a form because it catches arithmetically wrong answers, not because the decoy totals 44
a per-account vCPU quota is not an AWS service or capacity problem
